product_name: Driver Check In App — Administrative Module (The Hive, Schreiber Foods)

epics.title: Platform Foundation, Auth & Organization Setup
epics.description: Build the technical foundation: authentication, role management (Admin vs Standard), organization data model, and the HIVE navigation framework with tab system. At sprint end: admin users can log in, see the Administration menu, and manage organizations.
scope_in: HIVE Administration menu with dropdown navigation
In-app tab system (open pages in new HIVE tabs)
epics.definition_of_done: Admin can log in, see Administration menu, open Driver Check In Set Up in new tab, manage organizations. Non-admin cannot see admin menu.
epics.reasoning: Foundation must come first — auth, roles, and org model are prerequisites for all settings features. Navigation framework (menu + tabs) is needed before any admin page can be built. Deployable as v0.1.

features.title: Authentication & Session Management
features.description: Login page (email/password), JWT token issuance, session management, logout. Protected route middleware.

features.title: Role Management & Admin Authorization
features.description: Two roles: Admin and Standard User. Admin role gates Administration menu visibility and API access. Non-admin gets 403 on admin endpoints.

features.title: Organization Data Model & Management
features.description: Organization CRUD: name, address, phone (for {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE}). User-to-org assignment. Org context from authenticated user session.

features.title: HIVE Navigation Framework & Tab System
features.description: Administration menu with dropdown options. In-app tab system — selecting 'Driver Check In Set Up' opens a new tab with title 'Driver Check In Admin'. Tab management (open, close, switch).

epics.title: Settings Framework & Core Check-In Settings
epics.description: Build the settings page framework (toggle list, auto-save, validation) and implement the core driver identity settings. At sprint end: admin can view the settings page with toggles for Organization, Driver Name/ID/Phone/Truck, and Carrier Approval — all persisted per org.
scope_in: Settings list UI with toggle controls
Driver identity settings (Name, ID, Phone, Truck)
Settings data model and DB schema
epics.definition_of_done: Admin opens Driver Check In Admin tab, sees 6 settings with correct toggle states, can toggle Driver ID and Carrier Approval, changes auto-save on focus out, settings persist per org across page reloads.
epics.reasoning: Settings framework (toggle list, auto-save, validation, persistence) is the reusable foundation. Core identity settings are simple toggles — good for validating the framework. Deployable as v0.2.

features.title: Settings Page Framework & Toggle List
features.description: Settings page layout with list of settings. Each setting: name label, toggle control, optional input area, optional action button. Toggle ON/OFF controls setting state. Page loading skeleton while API fetches.

features.title: Auto-Save & Validation Engine
features.description: Auto-save all field values on focus out via PUT API. Validation on focus out: 'A value is required' (empty), 'Numbers only' (non-numeric), 'Invalid format' (bad format). Inline error display below field. Save confirmation indicator (brief checkmark).

features.title: Settings Data Model, API & Persistence
features.description: DB schema: settings table (setting_id, org_id, setting_name, toggle_state, input_value, updated_at, updated_by). API: GET /settings (all for org), PUT /settings/{id} (update toggle or value). Per-org isolation.

features.title: Organization Name & Driver Identity Settings
features.description: Organization Name: toggle always ON/disabled, input disabled/pre-populated from user org. Driver Name: toggle ON/disabled. Driver ID: toggle ON/active. Driver Phone: toggle ON/disabled. Truck Number: toggle ON/disabled. Carrier Approval: toggle ON/active.

features.title: Help Text Component
features.description: Reusable help text component displayed below configurable settings. Muted italic style. Linked to input via aria-describedby for screen readers.

epics.title: Advanced Settings — Temperature, Early Check In & Confirmation
epics.description: Implement the three complex settings with conditional inputs: Temperature Acknowledgement (alphanumeric input with validation), Early Check In (hours + instruction with defaults and placeholders), and Confirmation Step (customizable success message). At sprint end: all 10 settings fully functional with validation, help text, and auto-save.
scope_in: Temperature Acknowledgement setting with conditional input, alphanumeric validation, 'Invalid format' error
Early Check In setting with hours (numeric) and instruction (free text) inputs, default values, {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE} placeholder
Confirmation Step setting with customizable success text and default value
All three settings: conditional enable/disable based on toggle, help text, auto-save, validation
epics.definition_of_done: All 10 settings visible and functional. Temperature: toggle ON enables input, validation on focus out. Early Check In: toggle ON enables hours + instruction, defaults populated. Confirmation: toggle OFF disables input. All auto-save and validate correctly.
epics.reasoning: These three settings have the most complex behavior (conditional inputs, multiple validation rules, default values, help text). Building them after the framework (Sprint 2) means the toggle/save/validate infrastructure is already proven. Deployable as v0.3 with complete admin page.

features.title: Temperature Acknowledgement Setting
features.description: Toggle OFF by default, active. When ON: enable Temperature Range Requirements input (alphanumeric). Validation on focus out: 'Invalid format' for bad input, 'A value is required' if empty. Auto-save. Help text: 'Add the Temperature requirements to display during Check In via mobile app...'

features.title: Early Check In Setting with Hours & Instruction
features.description: Toggle OFF by default, active. When ON: enable (1) Allowed Early Hours input — numbers only, required, validation 'Numbers only'. (2) Early Instruction textarea — free text, required, default: 'Due to earlier arrival time...{TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE}'. Both auto-save on focus out. Help texts for both fields.

features.title: Confirmation Step Setting
features.description: Toggle ON by default, active. When ON: Confirmation Text input enabled with default: 'Driver Check In is successfully completed!...'. When OFF: input disabled. Validation: required when ON. Auto-save. Help text.

epics.title: QR Code Generation, PDF & Print
epics.description: Implement the QR Code generation flow: Generate button, modal with dynamic title, QR code image, Save as PDF download, Print dialog, and Close. Backend QR generation service. At sprint end: admin can generate, download, and print QR codes for facility driver check-in access.
scope_in: QR Code Check In Access toggle setting
QR modal: title 'QR Code for {ORG_NAME} Driver Check In Access'
epics.definition_of_done: Admin clicks Generate QR Code, modal shows with org-specific title and QR image. Save as PDF downloads file. Print opens system dialog. Close dismisses modal. QR regenerated on each click.
epics.reasoning: QR code is a self-contained feature with its own backend service (generation), frontend (modal), and output (PDF/print). Placed in Sprint 3 alongside advanced settings to deliver a complete admin page. Deployable as v0.3.

features.title: QR Code Generation Modal
features.description: Modal popup triggered by 'Generate QR Code' button. Title: 'QR Code for {ORG_NAME} Driver Check In Access'. Displays newly generated QR code image. Three action buttons: Save as PDF, Print, Close. Modal has focus trap, Escape to close.

features.title: QR Code Backend Generation Service
features.description: Backend endpoint: POST /api/v1/driver-checkin/qr-code?org_id={id}. Generates QR code image encoding the mobile check-in URL for the organization. Returns PNG image. New QR generated per request.

features.title: QR Code PDF Download & Print
features.description: Save as PDF: generate PDF containing QR code image + org name header, auto-download to user's computer. Print: trigger window.print() with print-optimized layout. Close: dismiss modal without action.

epics.title: Mobile App API & Hardening
epics.description: Build the mobile app read-only API for settings, implement toggle-to-mobile sync, and harden the application with security audit, accessibility audit, and error handling. At sprint end: mobile app can read enabled settings per org, complete security and accessibility compliance.
scope_in: Toggle state sync — OFF on admin disables in mobile
Error handling for API failures (save failures, network errors)
scope_out: QR code scanning in mobile app
epics.definition_of_done: Mobile API returns only enabled settings for org. Toggle OFF on admin → setting absent from mobile API response. Zero critical/high security findings. WCAG 2.1 AA audit passed. Audit log captures all setting changes.
epics.reasoning: Mobile API is the final integration piece — admin page must be complete first (Sprints 2-3). Hardening in final sprint ensures production readiness. Deployable as v1.0 GA.

features.title: Mobile App Settings API
features.description: Read-only endpoint: GET /api/v1/driver-checkin/settings/mobile?org_id={id}. Returns only settings where toggle is ON, with configured values. Different auth from admin API (mobile app token). Cached with short TTL.

features.title: Security & Accessibility Audit
features.description: SAST scan (zero critical/high), dependency vulnerability scan, WCAG 2.1 AA audit on all pages (keyboard nav, screen reader, focus management, color contrast). Fix all findings.

features.title: Error Handling, Audit Logging & Resilience
features.description: API failure handling: save failure shows error toast with retry. Network offline: queue saves, sync on reconnect. Audit logging: all setting changes logged (who, what, when, old/new value). Optimistic locking for concurrent edits.

delivery_summary: The Driver Check In Admin Module is decomposed into 5 epics across 4 sprints. Sprint 1 (EP-01) builds the foundation: auth, roles, org model, and HIVE navigation with tab system — deployable as v0.1. Sprint 2 (EP-02) delivers the settings framework with auto-save, validation, and the 6 core settings (Org, Driver Name/ID/Phone/Truck, Carrier Approval) — deployable as v0.2 with a functional admin page. Sprint 3 (EP-03 + EP-04) completes the admin page: 3 advanced settings (Temperature, Early Check In, Confirmation) plus QR code generation with PDF/Print — deployable as v0.3 with all 10 settings and QR capability. Sprint 4 (EP-05) adds the mobile API, security/accessibility audit, and production hardening — deployable as v1.0 GA. All 26 FRs covered across 18 features.
